about: Same five-step ladder as reviews.json (see its 'about'). {X} = the name he picks or types; {a}/{plural} = the kind of thing. 'against' marks the other side (the empty square on the card). · 7 Nov 2026: each slot has a 'label' (what the student sees: First reason, Second reason …) and a q that names the job exactly — 'adds a reason' was true of the other side too.
name: Essay
how: An essay in five sentences: one to introduce the topic, two reasons, the other side, and your conclusion. All about a topic you choose.

nameAsk.title: Which one?
nameAsk.aim: Pick a topic you have an opinion on. You’ll write about it.

notebook: Write your essay on {X} in five sentences, one per slot. Then check:
ticks: My first sentence introduces the topic.
Each reason has an example of my own.
My conclusion says clearly what I think.

ways.t: It is often argued that {X} can do more harm than good.
Nowadays, the question of {X} is one that divides opinion.
Many people have strong views on {X}, and it is easy to see why.

slots.q: Which one starts your first reason?

ways.t: In the first place, one clear advantage of {X} is that …
To begin with, it is worth pointing out that …
First of all, the main benefit of {X} is that …

slots.label: First reason

slots.q: Which one adds a second reason on the same side?

ways.t: What is more, another point in its favour is that …
In addition, many people believe that …
Furthermore, it is also true that …

slots.label: Second reason

slots.q: Which one turns to the other side?

ways.t: On the other hand, it could be argued that …
However, we should not forget that …
Nevertheless, one serious drawback of {X} is that …

slots.label: The other side

slots.q: Which one gives your final view?

ways.t: On balance, I firmly believe that …
All things considered, it seems to me that …
To sum up, I am convinced that …

slots.label: Conclusion
